ledger.x: c. 3300 BCE: the Early Harappan Ravi phase begins at Harappa; the Indus culture grows out of the farming villages of the Indus plain and Mehrgarh. 'The Early Harappan Ravi Phase, named after the nearby Ravi River, lasted from c. 3300 BCE until 2800 BCE'; infobox 'c. 3300 - c. 1300 BCE', 'Preceded by: Mehrgarh'. The…

c. 2800 BCE: the Kot Diji phase; Early Harappan settlement spreads along the Ghaggar-Hakra. 'Kot Diji Phase (2800-2600 BCE, Harappan 2)'; the Harappa page's Period 2 is the 'Kot Dijian (Early Harappan) phase, c. 2800 - 2600 BC'. The region is Cliopatria's -2700 shape less its -3000 shape: the page dates the phase, the…

c. 2600 BCE: the Mature Harappan (Integration Era) begins: planned cities, a script and standard weights. 'The mature phase of the Harappan civilisation lasted from c. 2600-1900 BCE', sub-phases Harappan 3A (2600-2450), 3B (2450-2200), 3C (2200-1900). A phase caption, not a border change.

c. 2500 BCE: Mohenjo-daro is built on the lower Indus and the great cities rise. 'Mohenjo-daro was built around 2500 BC' ('one of the largest settlements of the ancient Indus Valley Civilisation', 'an estimated population of at least 40,000 people'); a ruler found at Lothal is dated 2400 BCE on the same page. The…

c. 2300 BCE: the civilisation stands at its full extent. 'During its height the civilisation extended from Balochistan in the west to western Uttar Pradesh in the east'; the page dates the mature phase 2600-1900 BCE and gives no year for the height, so Cliopatria's -2300 is kept at confidence 1. A…

c. 1900 BCE: the Late Harappan (Localisation Era) begins; the cities decline and the population moves east. The mature phase ends in 1900 BCE; table 'Late Harappan 1900-1700 (Harappan 4)'; the Ghaggar-Hakra 'became seasonal around 4,000 years ago' and the reduced water supply was 'enough to cause the civilisation's…

c. 1900 BCE: the periphery empties; settlement localises in the Punjab, Sindh and Gujarat. 'Localisation Era / Late Harappan 1900-1300 BCE' with the 'Punjab Phase (Cemetery H); Jhukar Phase; Rangpur Phase' in 'Punjab; Sindh (Jhukar); Kachchh, Saurashtra, and mainland Gujarat (Rangpur)'. Harappa page: 'from around 2000…

c. 1700 BCE: Mohenjo-daro is abandoned. 'When the Indus civilisation went into sudden decline c. 1700 BCE, Mohenjo-daro was abandoned'. The periodisation page starts Harappan 5 in 1700; the Harappa page dates its own Late Harappan Phase c. 1800-1300 BC. The 40 km radius is the…

c. 1300 BCE: the Indus tradition ends; the Cemetery H, Ochre Coloured Pottery and Painted Grey Ware cultures follow on the same land. certainty.note: An archaeological culture, not a state: every edge is the spread of known sites, never a frontier; only the Arabian Sea coast is a hard line.
